items.stem: A weight lifter lifts a barbell as shown in the figure . List two forces that are acting on the barbell. Are these forces balanced if the weight lifter keeps the barbell steady?
items.answer: The two primary forces acting on the barbell are the downward gravitational force exerted by the Earth and the upward force applied by the weightlifter’s hands. Yes, if the weightlifter keeps the barbell completely steady, these two opposing forces are equal in magnitude and are balanced.

items.stem: A forensics student is investigating a case of a forged signature on a cheque. The suspect claims the signature was written using a standard black sketch pen found in the office. The student decides to test the ink. She places a tiny spot of ink from the cheque onto a thin strip of specialized filter paper. She carefully suspends the paper in a beaker containing a small amount of water, ensuring the ink spot sits just above the water level. After twenty minutes, she observes a beautiful band of blue, yellow, and red streaks climbing up the paper. QUESTIONS: (a) Identify the scientific technique being used by the forensics student to analyze the ink. (b) What can the student infer about the black ink based on the coloured streaks on the paper? (c) Explain the basic principle that allows the different colours to separate on the paper. (d) Why was it crucial for the student to keep the ink spot slightly above the water level at the beginning of the experiment?
items.answer: (a) The technique is paper chromatography. (b) The student can infer that the black ink is not a single pure substance, but a homogeneous mixture of multiple coloured components (dyes). (c) The separation is based on differences in the interactions of the components with the solvent and the paper. As the solvent (water) rises, it carries the dyes with it at different speeds, separating them. (d) If the ink spot was submerged in the water, the ink would simply dissolve into the bulk of the water at the bottom of the beaker instead of travelling up the paper strip.

items.stem: During a practical exam, a student accidentally pours acetone into a flask that contains pure distilled water. Acetone is highly miscible in water, resulting in a perfectly clear mixture. The teacher informs the student that the boiling point of water is 100 °C, while the boiling point of acetone is much lower, at 56 °C. She challenges the student to set up an apparatus to recover both liquids in their pure forms without losing either to the atmosphere. QUESTIONS: (a) Name the process the student should use to separate this mixture of miscible liquids. (b) Why is this specific separation process effective for the acetone and water mixture? (c) As the mixture is heated, which liquid will turn into vapour first, and why? (d) What is the role of the water condenser in this apparatus? (e) If the student had mixed two liquids with boiling points of 75 °C and 78 °C, could this exact same simple setup be used effectively? Explain.
items.answer: (a) The student should use the distillation process. (b) Distillation is effective because acetone and water are miscible liquids that boil without decomposition and have a sufficient difference in their boiling points (greater than 25 °C). (c) Acetone will vaporize first because it has a lower boiling point (56 °C) compared to water (100 °C). (d) The condenser cools the hot vapours of the vaporized liquid (acetone) by circulating cold water around it, turning the vapour back into a liquid so it can be collected in a separate flask. (e) No, simple distillation would not be effective because the difference in boiling points is less than 25 °C. items.stem: Using a horizontal force F, a table is moved across the floor at a constant velocity. How much is the frictional force exerted by the floor on the table?
items.answer: Since the table is moving at a constant velocity, the net force acting on it is zero. Therefore, the frictional force exerted by the floor on the table must be equal in magnitude and opposite in direction to the applied horizontal force F.

items.stem: For a ball moving on a smooth frictionless surface, choose the appropriate option that will make the following statements physically correct. (i) If no net force is applied on the ball, the velocity of the ball will remain the same/ increase/decrease. (ii) If a net force is applied on the ball in the direction of its motion, the magnitude of the velocity of the ball will remain the same/ increase/decrease. (iii) If a net force is applied on the ball in a direction opposite to the direction of its motion, the magnitude of the velocity of the ball will remain the same/increase/decrease.
items.answer: (i) remain the same According to Newton’s first law of motion, an object in motion will continue to move with a constant velocity unless acted upon by a net external force. (ii) increase A net force applied in the direction of motion provides an acceleration in the same direction, causing the velocity to increase. (iii) decrease A net force applied opposite to the motion causes deceleration, which reduces the magnitude of the ball’s velocity.

items.stem: Two blocks P and Q on a smooth horizontal surface are shown in Figure.a and Figure. b. Two forces of magnitudes 4 N and 5 N are acting in opposite directions on block P, while block Q is moving with a constant velocity. Which of the following statement is correct? (i) P experiences a net force and Q does not experience a net force. (ii) P does not experience a net force and Q experiences a net force. (iii) Both P and Q experience a net force. (iv) Neither P nor Q experiences a net force.
items.answer: Option (i) is correct. Block P experiences unbalanced forces (5 N right and 4 N left), resulting in a net force of 1 N. Block Q is moving with constant velocity, which implies its acceleration is zero, so it experiences zero net force according to Newton’s first law.

items.stem: While practising for the snake boat race (Vallum kalli in Kerala), 100 oarsmen are rowing a boat together. Out of these, 95 row backwards to propel the boat forward. But by mistake, 5 oarsmen row in the opposite direction. If each oarsman applies a horizontal force of 200 N, what is the net force on the snake boat? (Ignore drag forces, air friction, etc.)
items.answer: The 95 oarsmen rowing backwards propel the boat forward with a total force = 95 × 200 N = 19,000 N. The 5 mistaken oarsmen row forwards, pushing the boat backwards with a total force = 5 × 200 N = 1,000 N. The net force acting on the snake boat = 19,000 N - 1,000 N = 18,000 N in the forward direction. 5. When a net force acts on an object, we observe that the object accelerates: (i) opposite to the direction of force, with acceleration proportional to the force acting on the object. (ii) opposite to the direction of force, with acceleration proportional to the mass of the object. Exploring Mixtures and their Separation

items.stem: (a) A concentrated liquid pesticide spray is heavily diluted by mixing 25 mL of the active pesticide with pure water to make a total volume of 500 mL. Calculate its final volume by volume percentage? (b) Explain exactly what an emulsion is, providing an everyday example, and explain how emulsifying agents function?
items.answer: (a) To calculate the concentration properly, use the standard volume by volume percentage formula. The volume of the solute, which is the concentrated pesticide, equals twenty- five millilitres. The total combined volume of the final aqueous solution is given as five hundred millilitres. The mass by volume percentage equals the solute volume divided by the total solution volume, multiplied by one hundred. Therefore, dividing twenty-five by five hundred yields zero point zero five. Multiplying this by one hundred results in a final concentration of exactly five percent. (b) An emulsion is a distinct category of colloidal mixture where both the dispersed phase and the surrounding dispersion medium are mutually immiscible liquids. Everyday milk is a perfect example. Emulsifying agents, such as natural milk proteins, effectively stabilize these mixtures by preventing the suspended liquid droplets from aggressively coalescing and separating into distinct layers.
